hints: Focus on what Fehling's solution tells you, it only gives a red precipitate with aldehydes, not ketones.
Deduce the alcohol classes: W must be primary since it forms an aldehyde Y, while X must be secondary since it forms a ketone Z.
Recall the iodoform condition needs a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group in the alcohol, so check which C4 secondary alcohol contains this.
walkthrough:
**Use Fehling's to identify Y and Z**

Think of Fehling's as an aldehyde detector. A red precipitate means aldehyde, no precipitate means ketone.

So Y is an aldehyde and Z is a ketone.

**Work back to alcohol classes W and X**

Remember the oxidation pattern: primary alcohol to aldehyde, secondary alcohol to ketone, tertiary alcohol resists oxidation.

$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \quad , \quad \text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone}$$ 
So W is a primary alcohol and X is a secondary alcohol.

**Apply the iodoform test rule**

The yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline $\text{I}_2$ needs a methyl group next to the functional carbon.

$$\text{positive group: } \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \text{ for alcohols, } \text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{ for carbonyls}$$

**Check the C4 isomers**

The only oxidisable secondary $\text{C}_4$ alcohol is butan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It clearly contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$.

Primary $\text{C}_4$ alcohols are butan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, and 2-methylpropan-1-ol. Neither contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$. So only X gives the yellow precipitate.

options.A: There is enough data. Fehling's identifies the carbonyl type, which identifies the alcohol class, and the formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$ limits the structures enough to judge the iodoform test.
options.B: W only is wrong. W is primary and oxidises to an aldehyde Y. The C4 primary aldehydes are $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ and $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCHO}$, neither is ethanal, and W itself lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group.
options.C: X only is correct. X is secondary and must be butan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group and so gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline $\text{I}_2$.
options.D: Neither is wrong. It is tempting to think only ethanol and methyl ketones give iodoform, but secondary alcohols of the form $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)R}$ also give it. Butan-2-ol is a classic positive example.
